questions: Do the iteration 9 metrics match iteration 6 or 8 (score 36.3097) to four decimals on all tracks? If so, geometry is exhausted for this controller, and the Integrator should move to kd (about 0.2) or base_speed without further geometry changes.
Does wheel_track 0.10 m at kp 3.0 lower max_error below 0.06 m, or reduce line_loss_events below one on the oval or s-bend?
Does the narrower track raise slalom steering_oscillation above the 0.16 seen at wheel_track 0.12 m? If so, the fix is kd damping, not a wider track.
Please report per-step telemetry for one trial per track: the step and progress at which the first line loss begins, and whether it occurs at the course start or at a specific bend.

intent: Test whether a narrower wheel track (0.10 m) adds enough yaw response at kp 3.0 to clear the line-loss event on the oval and s-bend, using the widest 16 mm row (±0.04 m, y = 0.07 m) at the best-scoring mass of 0.8 kg. This isolates wheel_track against the iteration-8 and iteration-6 baselines (score 36.3097). The Integrator should keep the controller weights scaled to the ±0.04 m layout (x/0.03 relative to the ±0.03 m layout, as in iteration 8).
learning: Iterations 0 to 8 show that spread (0.02 to 0.04 m), footprint (12 to 16 mm), wheel_track (0.10 to 0.12 m at kp 2 and 0.12 m at kp 3), wheel_radius (0.03 to 0.04 m), lead (0.05 to 0.07 m) and mass (0.5 to 0.8 kg) leave max_error at 0.060 to 0.062 m and line loss at one per trial on the oval and s-bend. Only kp 3.0 moved the score, and only on the slalom. Iteration 8 matched iteration 6 to four decimals, which confirms that the sensor row is not the limit. Iteration 9 is the last geometry test; if it matches the baseline, the remaining levers are controller damping (kd) and base_speed, and I will not spend further iterations on geometry.
rationale: Iteration 8 (sensors at x = ±0.04 m, 16 mm footprints, y = 0.07 m, mass 0.8 kg, wheel_track 0.12 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m) returned score 36.3097 and metrics identical to iteration 6 to four decimals on all three tracks: max_error 0.0614, 0.0611 and 0.0694 m, one line-loss event per trial, and no finishes. Widening the row removed nothing, so the row reach is not the limit. Across spread, footprint, track, radius, lead and mass, the only change that moved the score is controller gain (kp 3.0), and it moved only the slalom. The line-loss mechanism on the oval and s-bend is unchanged. The Integrator's rule (c) for this case is to test wheel_track 0.10 m on the new row to see whether more yaw response helps. Iteration 3 tested 0.10 m only at kp 2.0, so the combination with kp 3.0 is untested. I therefore keep the ±0.04 m, 16 mm row at y = 0.07 m with mass 0.8 kg and change only wheel_track from 0.12 m to 0.10 m. This is the last geometry test I can justify. If the metrics match iteration 6 again, geometry is exhausted for this controller and the remaining levers are controller damping (kd near 0.2) and base_speed, which are the Integrator's to test. Mass 0.5 kg is rejected: it cut the score by 0.67 points by lowering slalom progress. Expected result: a yaw-response change should show up as a change in max_error or line_loss_events on the oval and s-bend. Most likely the metrics stay at the baseline.
